jp: 朝[あさ]起[お]きて、カーテンを{開[あ]けました|tr-aku}。
en: I got up in the morning and opened the curtains.
why: The curtains are the object (を) of someone's action, so the transitive 開ける is needed.

jp: 玄関[げんかん]のドアが急[きゅう]に{開[あ]きました|tr-aku}。
en: The front door suddenly opened.
why: The door is the subject (が) and nobody is acting on it, so the intransitive 開く fits.

jp: 寝[ね]る前[まえ]に、部屋[へや]の電気[でんき]を{消[け]しました|tr-aku}。
en: Before going to bed, I turned off the light in my room.
why: Someone switches the light off (を), so the transitive 消す is needed.

jp: 停電[ていでん]で、家中[いえじゅう]の電気[でんき]が{消[き]えました|tr-aku}。
en: Because of a power cut, all the lights in the house went out.
why: The lights are the subject (が) and go out by themselves, so intransitive 消える fits.

jp: 母[はは]は出[で]かける前[まえ]に、窓[まど]を{閉[し]めました|tr-aku}。
en: Before going out, my mother closed the windows.
why: Mother acts on the windows (を), so the transitive 閉める is needed.

jp: 風[かぜ]が強[つよ]くて、ドアが勝手[かって]に{閉[し]まりました|tr-aku}。
en: The wind was strong, and the door closed by itself.
why: The door closed by itself (が, 勝手に), so the intransitive 閉まる fits.

jp: 部屋[へや]に入[はい]ると、テレビが{ついていました|tr-aku}。
en: When I entered the room, the TV was on.
why: The TV is the subject (が) in a resulting state, so intransitive ついている is needed.

jp: 夕食[ゆうしょく]の準備[じゅんび]を、母[はは]が六時[ろくじ]に{始[はじ]めました|tr-hajimaru}。
en: My mother started preparing dinner at six.
why: Mother begins the preparation (を), so the transitive 始める is needed.

jp: 朝[あさ]のニュース番組[ばんぐみ]が七時[しちじ]に{始[はじ]まります|tr-hajimaru}。
en: The morning news program starts at seven.
why: The program is the subject (が) and starts on its own schedule, so intransitive 始まる fits.

jp: 台所[だいどころ]の時計[とけい]が{止[と]まっています|tr-hajimaru}。
en: The clock in the kitchen has stopped.
why: The clock is the subject (が) and nobody is stopping it, so intransitive 止まる fits.

jp: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]が三日[みっか]も{続[つづ]いています|tr-hajimaru}。
en: Rainy days have continued for three days now.
why: Rainy days (が) simply go on, so intransitive 続く fits; 続ける needs a person acting.

jp: 洗濯[せんたく]が{終[お]わりました|tr-hajimaru}。
en: The laundry is finished.
why: The laundry (が) has ended by itself, so intransitive 終わる fits; 終える needs a doer and を.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は玄関[げんかん]の前[まえ]で足[あし]を{止[と]めました|tr-hajimaru}。
en: My little brother stopped in front of the entrance.
why: He stops his own foot (を), so the transitive 止める is needed.

jp: 朝[あさ]の光[ひかり]が窓[まど]から部屋[へや]に{入[はい]って|tr-hairu}きます。
en: The morning light comes into the room through the window.
why: Light (が) moves in by itself, so intransitive 入る fits; 入れる needs someone and を.

jp: 買[か]ってきた牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]を冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]に{入[い]れました|tr-hairu}。
en: I put the milk I had bought into the fridge.
why: Someone puts the milk (を) in, so the transitive 入れる is needed.

jp: 洗濯物[せんたくもの]が風[かぜ]で床[ゆか]に{落[お]ちました|tr-hairu}。
en: The laundry fell onto the floor in the wind.
why: The laundry (が) fell by itself, so intransitive 落ちる fits.

jp: 子[こ]どもが皿[さら]を床[ゆか]に{落[お]としてしまいました|tr-hairu}。
en: The child dropped a plate on the floor.
d: 落[お]ちてしまいました
why: The child drops the plate (を), so the transitive 落とす is needed.

jp: 妹[いもうと]は二階[にかい]に{上[あ]がって|tr-hairu}いきました。
en: My younger sister went up to the second floor.
why: She moves herself upstairs with no object, so intransitive 上がる fits.

jp: 部屋[へや]が暑[あつ]いので、エアコンの温度[おんど]を{下[さ]げました|tr-hairu}。
en: The room was hot, so I lowered the air conditioner's temperature.
why: I act on the temperature (を), so the transitive 下げる is needed.

jp: 母[はは]は毎朝[まいあさ]、ごみを外[そと]に{出[だ]します|tr-hairu}。
en: My mother puts the trash outside every morning.
why: The trash is the object (を) put out by someone, so the transitive 出す is needed.

jp: 弟[おとうと]がコップを{割[わ]りました|tr-kowareru}。
en: My little brother broke a glass.
why: He is the agent acting on the glass (を), so the transitive 割る is needed.

jp: 台所[だいどころ]で皿[さら]が{割[わ]れていました|tr-kowareru}。
en: A plate was broken in the kitchen.
why: The plate (が) is in a broken state, so intransitive 割れる is needed.

jp: 掃除機[そうじき]が{壊[こわ]れました|tr-kowareru}。
en: The vacuum cleaner broke.
why: The vacuum cleaner is the subject (が) and simply stopped working, so 壊れる fits.

jp: 父[ちち]は古[ふる]くなったテレビを{直[なお]しました|tr-kowareru}。
en: My father repaired the old TV.
why: Father acts on the TV (を), so the transitive 直す is needed.

jp: 洗濯物[せんたくもの]を干[ほ]す紐[ひも]が{切[き]れました|tr-kowareru}。
en: The cord for hanging the laundry snapped.
why: The cord (が) snapped by itself, so intransitive 切れる fits.

jp: 子[こ]どもがジュースをこぼして、床[ゆか]を{汚[よご]しました|tr-kowareru}。
en: The child spilled juice and made the floor dirty.
why: The child makes the floor (を) dirty, so the transitive 汚す is needed.

jp: 強[つよ]い風[かぜ]で傘[かさ]が{折[お]れました|tr-kowareru}。
en: The umbrella broke in the strong wind.
why: The umbrella (が) bent and snapped from the wind, so intransitive 折れる fits.

jp: 今度[こんど]の家族旅行[かぞくりょこう]の行[い]き先[さき]が{決[き]まりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The destination of our next family trip has been decided.
why: The destination (が) is settled and no decider is named, so intransitive 決まる fits.

jp: 家族[かぞく]で相談[そうだん]して、夏休[なつやす]みの予定[よてい]を{決[き]めました|tr-kimaru}。
en: We talked it over as a family and decided our summer vacation plans.
why: The family decides the plans (を), so the transitive 決める is needed.

jp: 母[はは]はカーテンの色[いろ]を{変[か]えました|tr-kimaru}。
en: My mother changed the color of the curtains.
why: Mother changes the color (を), so the transitive 変える is needed.

jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しをして、生活[せいかつ]が{変[か]わりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: We moved house, and our life changed.
why: Life (が) changed as a result with no one acting on it, so intransitive 変わる fits.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]の朝[あさ]、家族[かぞく]が居間[いま]に{集[あつ]まりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: On Sunday morning, the family gathered in the living room.
why: The family (が) comes together by itself, so intransitive 集まる fits.

jp: 探[さが]していた鍵[かぎ]が、ソファの下[した]で{見[み]つかりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The key I had been looking for was found under the sofa.
why: The key (が) turned up, so intransitive 見つかる fits.

jp: 弟[おとうと]はベッドの下[した]で、なくした消[け]しゴムを{見[み]つけました|tr-kimaru}。
en: My little brother found the eraser he had lost under the bed.
why: He finds the eraser (を), so the transitive 見つける is needed.

jp: 夕食[ゆうしょく]の前[まえ]に、テーブルに皿[さら]を{並[なら]べました|tr-narabu}。
en: Before dinner, I set the plates on the table.
why: I arrange the plates (を), so the transitive 並べる is needed.

jp: 玄関[げんかん]に家族[かぞく]の靴[くつ]が{並[なら]んでいます|tr-narabu}。
en: The family's shoes are lined up at the entrance.
why: The shoes (が) are in a lined-up state, so intransitive 並ぶ is needed.

jp: 荷物[にもつ]が午後[ごご]に家[いえ]に{届[とど]きました|tr-narabu}。
en: The package arrived at our house in the afternoon.
why: The package (が) arrives and is the subject, so 届く fits; 届ける needs a deliverer.

jp: 作[つく]りすぎて、カレーが{残[のこ]りました|tr-narabu}。
en: I made too much, so some curry was left over.
why: The curry (が) is left over by itself, so intransitive 残る fits.

jp: 父[ちち]は妹[いもうと]を自転車[じてんしゃ]の後[うし]ろに{乗[の]せました|tr-narabu}。
en: My father put my little sister on the back of the bicycle.
why: Father puts his sister (を) on, so the transitive 乗せる is needed.

jp: 壁[かべ]に時計[とけい]を{かけました|tr-narabu}。
en: I hung a clock on the wall.
why: I hang the clock (を), so the transitive かける is needed.

jp: 母[はは]は寝[ね]ている弟[おとうと]を{起[お]こしました|tr-okiru}。
en: My mother woke up my sleeping little brother.
why: Mother wakes someone else (を), so the transitive 起こす is needed.

jp: 祖父[そふ]は庭[にわ]で野菜[やさい]を{育[そだ]てています|tr-okiru}。
en: My grandfather is growing vegetables in the garden.
why: Grandfather raises vegetables (を), so the transitive 育てる is needed.

jp: 庭[にわ]のトマトが大[おお]きく{育[そだ]ちました|tr-okiru}。
en: The tomatoes in the garden grew big.
why: The tomatoes (が) grew by themselves, so intransitive 育つ fits.

jp: 食費[しょくひ]が毎月[まいつき]少[すこ]しずつ{増[ふ]えています|tr-okiru}。
en: Our food costs are rising little by little every month.
why: Food costs (が) go up on their own, so intransitive 増える fits.

jp: 健康[けんこう]のために、母[はは]は食事[しょくじ]の野菜[やさい]を{増[ふ]やしました|tr-okiru}。
en: For her health, my mother increased the vegetables in her meals.
why: Mother increases the vegetables (を), so the transitive 増やす is needed.

jp: 電気代[でんきだい]を{減[へ]らす|tr-okiru}ために、こまめに電気[でんき]を消[け]しています。
en: I switch off the lights often to cut down the electricity bill.
why: The bill is the object (を) of an intended action, so the transitive 減らす is needed.

jp: 夏[なつ]、母[はは]はスイカを冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]で{冷[ひ]やします|tr-okiru}。
en: In summer, my mother chills a watermelon in the fridge.
why: Mother chills the watermelon (を), so the transitive 冷やす is needed.

jp: お風呂[ふろ]に入[はい]ったので、体[からだ]が{温[あたた]まりました|tr-okiru}。
en: I took a bath, so my body warmed up.
why: The body (が) warms up by itself, so intransitive 温まる fits.

jp: 朝[あさ]、母[はは]が弟[おとうと]のために牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]を{温[あたた]めました|tr-okiru}。
en: In the morning, my mother warmed up some milk for my little brother.
d: 温[あたた]まっています
why: Mother heats the milk (を), so the transitive 温める is needed.
